title: Bolshie Tigani cemetery
fact_summary: A 9th–10th century cemetery in the Volga region where archaeologists identified a Hungarian component in the burial customs and grave goods.

place.label: Volga region
place.note: Pin placed by Claude in the region the study names ('Russia (Volga)'). The cemetery's exact position has not been checked.

claims.text: A 2022 study lists Bolshie Tigani in Russia (Volga), dates it to the 9th–10th centuries, and assigns it to the Late Kushnarenkovo/Karayakupovo culture of the early Volga-Kama Bulghar period.
claims.certainty_reason: One tier B study; the excavation report has not been opened.

claims.text: The study says the maternal lineages of Bolshie Tigani connect it to sites of the later Chiyalik culture (11th–14th centuries), with numerous identical maternal lineages between them.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: In the cemeteries of Bolshie Tigani and Tankeevka, a Hungarian ethnic component can be identified from burial customs and grave goods.

held_by.who: Szeifert et al. (2022), reporting archaeological research

claims.certainty_reason: Reported in one tier B study; the archaeological publications behind it have not been opened.

dating_methods.text: Dated to the 9th–10th centuries in the study's site table.

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
